statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Nasdaq-100 complex is inside the CME weekend halt, so no quoting price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor.
recommendation: Tail stays far below the block threshold at a closed-venue floor of 4-5%, so the deterministic mapping holds EA_ON and green across all 24 published hours. Stress drifts from 40% to 48%, entering the elevated band from 23:00 UTC on 5 September, to reflect hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across the halt. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt; the entire 24-hour horizon ends about eleven hours before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release shows August nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year. Reuters reported the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting rising to 58.4% from 49.4% the previous day, while the H.15 release carries the two-year Treasury yield at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%. The VIX settled at 14.53, up 1.47% but still a low absolute base. Sector behaviour was narrow rather than uniform: the semiconductor complex advanced strongly, with the SOXX ETF outpacing QQQ by roughly three percentage points as Micron, AMD, Intel and Arm all gained, while megacaps were mixed to lower with Tesla down 5.9%, Apple down 2.5% and Microsoft down 2.0%. Rotational, divergent leadership of that kind argues against a single one-way index path. Energy remains the largest unpriced variable: Reuters reports Brent at $92.68 and WTI at $91.48 after weekly gains of 7.6% and nearly 10%, driven by resumed US-Iran military exchanges in the seventh month of that conflict, Strait of Hormuz transits running near four vessels against a ten-day average close to fifteen, and a record US average diesel price of $5.85 per gallon. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to restart at 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, so every hour in this assessment window falls inside the halt. Because no venue quotes NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD, mean reversion can neither succeed nor fail and the strategy-relevant Tail is structurally near zero throughout. Stress is scored higher and drifting because hawkish rate repricing, the energy premium and an open two-sided geopolitical headline window all accumulate without a price to absorb them; that exposure would most plausibly arrive as a discrete restart gap rather than as a persistent no-retracement trend, which is why it is carried in Stress rather than in Tail. Confidence is held at 85% because index level, range, yields, oil, volatility, catalysts and the seven-day calendar are all verified; the single missing input is the live price path, and it is missing by venue schedule rather than through thin evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the second half of the August payroll session and the first sixteen hours of the CME weekend halt. Tail peaked at 24% with Stress at 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 56,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered. Mode moved to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, and by 20:00 UTC Tail was 12% with Stress at 48%. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with Stress at 38-39% and mode normal. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment and every hour mapped to EA_ON except the two WATCH hours around the release.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 40% to 48%, entering the elevated band from 23:00 UTC on 5 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat, a Strait of Hormuz energy premium that lifted WTI roughly 10% on the week, and an open two-sided weekend headline window. Confidence eases from 85% to 80% purely through the ageing of Friday-anchored evidence. The horizon ends around 11:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly eleven hours before the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex restart, so the first live price-path evaluation belongs to a later run.
